page.title: Webinar Production Agency: When to Hire and What to Expect
page.description: Learn when to hire a webinar production agency, what they deliver, typical costs, timelines, platforms, and how to choose the right partner for virtual events.
page.h1: When should a founder hire a webinar production agency?
page.definition: A webinar production agency is a specialist team that plans, runs and records live virtual events on your chosen platform, handling run of show, speaker rehearsals, branded assets, live moderation, backup streams and post-event editing so internal teams can focus on content and revenue.
page.quick_answer: Hire an agency when your webinar has commercial stakes, sponsors, multiple speakers, live demos or complex follow-up workflows that exceed your team's capacity to produce reliably.

sections.h2: What does a webinar production agency actually deliver?

blocks.p: A production agency owns the end-to-end live experience while you keep control of the platform licence and the content strategy.

ul: Run of show with timed cues and contingency plans
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the real platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Live producer directing cameras, screens and transitions
Backup stream ready to switch instantly
Edited recording and short clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: How much does a produced webinar cost?

blocks.p: Pricing follows the event complexity, not the platform licence, and agencies typically quote per production rather than per hour.
West Peek Productions does not sell event software. It produces events on the platform you choose and can help you choose it.

sections.h2: What is the typical timeline from brief to live?

blocks.p: A single webinar moves from approved brief to live in three to four weeks; a summit or online conference needs six to eight weeks of management.

ol: Full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Technical check 60 minutes before going live
Live production with backup stream active
Replay and clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours
Reporting and follow-up handoff to marketing

sections.h2: Which platforms do agencies work with?

blocks.p: Production is platform-agnostic; the crew joins the licence you already own such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard and runs the show inside it.

The platform is not the production. Someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: How do you choose the right production partner?

blocks.p: Match the agency's staffing model and tool stack to your event size and internal workflow.

ul: Ask for a sample run of show and speaker brief template
Confirm they provide a dedicated show caller for summits
Verify backup stream hardware and encoder redundancy
Check integration with your registration tool (Eventbrite, Cvent) and CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce)
Request a post-event reporting sample with GA4 and HubSpot metrics
Ensure they operate on your platform licence, not a proprietary one

sections.h2: What staffing model fits your event size?

blocks.p: Staffing scales with complexity; a simple webinar needs one producer while a summit requires a full crew.

head: Event size
Core roles
rows: Show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator
Show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator, venue AV liaison

faq.q: Do I need a separate platform licence if I hire a production agency?
faq.a: Yes. Platform and production are two purchases: the platform is software; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. The agency works on the licence you already own.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a production agency for a summit?
faq.a: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. A webinar needs three to four weeks lead time.

faq.q: Can the agency help with speaker rehearsals and slide reviews?
faq.a: Standard deliverables include speaker brief and rehearsal on the real platform, branded slide template and lower thirds, and a full rehearsal two to five days before the live date.

faq.q: What happens if the primary stream fails during the event?
faq.a: A backup stream runs in parallel and the producer can switch instantly. The agency also conducts a technical check 60 minutes before going live to verify both paths.

faq.q: How quickly do I get the recording and clips after the event?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours, while attendees still remember the event. Edited recordings and short clips are part of the standard delivery package.
